{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-tn","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"2971ac3ebf37ee17c6fdde678154c0ba541237d224115f9862fbeab12f2d01a6","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-tn-class-d:lineage:105","source_registry_sha256":"8b0b6a068a0aa720d419171b5007a2610ed6c5012eeff522b57713cf9226eb71","source_liveness_sha256":"d27b9a94f03ec29d960b8eea38966606a7d3fdb703ad30b19ecd93f9bc70d0c7"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Special driving conditions and your vehicle confusables and continuation details","heading":"C2 — Confusable pairs and continuation facts: evasive turn hand moves, braking before a turn, deer warning signs and headlights, antilock practice, careful versus careless drivers, vision, glasses, fatigue and health tips, vehicle checks, exhaust, cooling and loose objects, traffic flow and trouble spots","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Confusable pairs and continuation facts: evasive turn hand moves, braking before a turn, deer warning signs and headlights, antilock practice, careful versus careless drivers, vision, glasses, fatigue and health tips, vehicle checks, exhaust, cooling and loose objects, traffic flow and trouble spots
Confusable pairs and continuation facts; each block ties to one manual page, and any hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec15-R01 | anchor: A01
Read your vehicle owner's manual to learn how its antilock braking system works, since antilock brakes let you stop without skidding. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec15-R02 | anchor: A01
For a quick evasive turn to the left, the right hand swings from 3 o'clock toward 9 o'clock as far as needed while the left hand slides toward the bottom of the wheel to steady the grip. [A01]
Why it matters: group evasive steering; confusable left turn versus right turn hand moves.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec15-R03 | anchor: A01
As you clear the hazard, turn the wheel back to the right to regain your lane, then left just enough to straighten out, returning your hands to 9 and 3; for a quick right turn, mirror every step. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec15-R04 | anchor: A02
Braking before a quick turn without antilock brakes slows the car and shifts weight onto the front tires, which lets it turn faster. [A02]
Why it matters: group braking and turning; confusable with versus without antilock brakes.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec15-R05 | anchor: A02
Animal crashes can happen in any season and with any animal, from opossums and rabbits to dogs, and while many deer crashes occur at night, they can happen at any hour. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec15-R06 | anchor: A02
No foolproof method has been found to keep deer and other wild animals off highways. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec15-R07 | anchor: A02
To avoid deer, heed deer crossing signs, look far down the road and well off to each side, and at night use high beams when you can to light the road edges. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec15-R08 | anchor: A02
Scan the roadsides for your headlights reflecting in a deer's eyes. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec15-R09 | anchor: A02
If you have time to avoid an animal ahead, slow down, tap your brakes to warn drivers behind you, and sound your horn. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec15-R10 | anchor: A02
Deer tend to fixate on headlights, so flashing your lights at one may make it freeze in the road. [A02]
Why it matters: group deer and headlights; confusable high beams for seeing versus flashing at a deer.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec15-R11 | anchor: A02
If no vehicle is close behind you, brake hard for an animal but do not lock the wheels into a skid. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec15-R12 | anchor: A02
If you hit a domestic pet near homes, try to let the owner know if you can. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec15-R13 | anchor: A02
With antilock brakes, keep your foot firmly on the pedal despite the pulsing and noise, because easing off ruins the system's advantage. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec15-R14 | anchor: A03
Use the antilock system's nonskid ability to steer around the obstacle that made you brake, and keep steering to a safe place once past it. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec15-R15 | anchor: A03
To practice antilock braking, use a big empty lot without curbs or many light poles, drive about 20 mph, slam the brakes and steer, later steering around a cardboard box as a target. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec15-R16 | anchor: A03
Keep at least a two-second cushion behind the vehicle ahead, and more when conditions are hazardous. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec15-R17 | anchor: A03
A good driver takes pride in caring for the vehicle, obeys traffic laws and respects others, while a careless driver neglects all three. [A03]
Why it matters: group driver attitude; confusable careful versus careless driver.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec15-R18 | anchor: A03
The manual attributes about 160,000 crashes reported to the Department of Safety each year to poor driving habits. [A03]
Why it matters: dated statistic; dynamic.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec15-R19 | anchor: A03
Being in shape to drive means seeing clearly, being rested, being free of drugs, and being healthy and emotionally fit. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec15-R20 | anchor: A03
Everyone sees worse at night, and some drivers struggle with the glare of oncoming headlights. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec15-R21 | anchor: A04
If you have trouble seeing at night, limit night driving to what is necessary and be very careful when you do. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec15-R22 | anchor: A04
Judging distance and speed takes practice and matters most when merging and when judging gaps to pass on two-lane roads. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec15-R23 | anchor: A04
If you need glasses or contacts, wear them even on short trips, and keep a spare pair in the vehicle. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec15-R24 | anchor: A04
Hearing helps you notice horns, sirens and screeching tires, and hearing-impaired drivers can compensate with their vision. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec15-R25 | anchor: A04
To avoid fatigue, get a normal night's sleep, eat lightly before a long trip, avoid medicine that causes drowsiness, and try not to drive when you would normally be asleep. [A04]
Why it matters: group fatigue; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec15-R26 | anchor: A04
If you feel unwell, even from a stiff neck, cough or sore leg, let someone else drive. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec15-R27 | anchor: A04
A diabetic on insulin should stay off the road whenever an insulin reaction, blackout, convulsion or shock is possible, for example after skipping a meal. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec15-R28 | anchor: A04
People with heart disease, high blood pressure or circulation problems who risk blackouts, fainting or a heart attack should not drive, and anyone treated for a heart condition should ask a doctor about driving. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec15-R29 | anchor: A04
No one, regardless of skill or experience, can drive safely when buzzed or impaired by alcohol or drugs. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec15-R30 | anchor: A05
Have a mechanic check your brakes if they seem weak, are noisy, smell odd or the pedal sinks to the floor. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0114]

FACT_ID: sec15-R31 | anchor: A05
Check turn signals, brake lights, taillights and headlights from outside the vehicle. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0114]

FACT_ID: sec15-R32 | anchor: A05
Batteries run down faster in cold or damp weather, and keeping jumper cables in the car can get you started again. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0114]

FACT_ID: sec15-R33 | anchor: A05
Repair or replace a damaged windshield, since cracked glass can break in a minor collision, and replace wiper blades that no longer clear the glass. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0114]

FACT_ID: sec15-R34 | anchor: A05
Check the non-freezing washer fluid level each time you fill up with gas, and clean the windshield at gas stops so sun or headlights do not blur your view. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0114]

FACT_ID: sec15-R35 | anchor: A05
Unbalanced tires and low pressure wear tires faster, waste fuel and make the vehicle harder to steer and stop. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0114]

FACT_ID: sec15-R36 | anchor: A05
If you have put on aftermarket tires of a different size, ask the tire maker or installer for the right pressure, since the door-jamb figure no longer applies. [A05]
Why it matters: group tire pressure; confusable original tires versus aftermarket tires.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0114]

FACT_ID: sec15-R37 | anchor: A06
If the car keeps bouncing after a bump or a stop, or is hard to control, have a mechanic check the shocks and suspension. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec15-R38 | anchor: A06
When idling for a long time, open a window for fresh air, and never sleep or sit with the engine running during an extended rest stop. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec15-R39 | anchor: A06
Check the radiator only when the engine is cool, and keep coolant at the level the owner's manual recommends to prevent overheating or freezing. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec15-R40 | anchor: A06
Keep loose objects off the floor where they could roll under the brake pedal, and secure items that could hit someone in a sudden stop. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec15-R41 | anchor: A06
Use the horn only as a warning to others. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec15-R42 | anchor: A06
Vehicles moving the same direction at the same speed cannot hit one another, and multi-vehicle crashes often happen when drivers go faster or slower than traffic. [A06]
Why it matters: group traffic flow; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec15-R43 | anchor: A06
Slow down where people and traffic gather, such as when brake lights come on several cars ahead, in shopping centers and downtown areas, and at rush hour. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec15-R44 | anchor: A06
On narrow bridges and in tunnels, approaching vehicles pass closer together, so adjust your speed [A06] [A07].
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec15-R45 | anchor: A07
At railroad crossings, make sure no train is coming and you have room to get across, and slow down on bumpy crossings. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec15-R46 | anchor: A07
Good drivers review the manual periodically for law changes and study the driver manual of any new state they move to, even when no test is required. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0116]
